description: Stage 3 admission currently treats parked idle flows (refused, runner process gone) as active holders of their planned touch set, causing chain-blocking across unrelated resumes and wasting slot capacity.
goal: Update Stage 3 admission in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/admission.py, admission_decision.py, admission_lock.py, admission_order.py, admission_record.py, and admission_state.py so a parked flow releases its touch set: admission blocks only on open PRs and flows with a live runner process, ordering parked flows by original admission order so when two parked flows resume at once the first claims the touch set and the second refuses with a named live blocker. Add hermetic unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/flow/test_admission.py, tests/flow/test_admission_lock.py, tests/flow/test_admission_order.py, and tests/flow/test_admission_base_files.py covering both cases while keeping all existing tests passing under uv run pytest and uv run task lint, and keeping holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json untouched and every module within its budget. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: Letting parked flows release their touch sets prevents one waiting PR from chain-blocking queued flows and lets the first resumed flow claim its touch set deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: A test: candidate overlapping a parked (no live runner) flow is admitted.
A test: two parked flows resuming at once admit exactly one, the other refuses with a named live blocker.

All changes remain within apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/admission.py, admission_decision.py, admission_lock.py, admission_order.py, admission_record.py, admission_state.py, tests/flow/test_admission.py, tests/flow/test_admission_lock.py, tests/flow/test_admission_order.py, and tests/flow/test_admission_base_files.py (holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json untouched), uv run pytest and uv run task lint pass, and code is self-explaining (no docstrings; only '# why:' comments).
